c.tagline: Danube river town crowned by the world's tallest church spire

taxi.fareNote: Standard German metered taxis; ranks at the Hauptbahnhof and Münsterplatz, or booked by phone/app

emergency.note: Fast, reliable emergency response; English-speaking operators are common

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Fischerviertel: Half-timbered houses on the Blau canals

hood_desc: Ulm's compact medieval core, dominated by the 161.5-meter spire of Ulm Minster, the tallest church tower on Earth. Cobblestone squares, the ornate town hall, and Einstein's birthplace memorial all sit within a few minutes' walk of each other. It's the obvious first stop and stays lively with cafes and shops.

The Fishermen's and Tanners' Quarter, a picture-postcard tangle of half-timbered houses along the little Blau River canals just south of the Altstadt. Leaning, centuries-old buildings house restaurants and boutique hotels, making it one of the most photographed corners of southern Germany.

A mixed residential and nightlife district along the Danube promenade, popular with students and young professionals for its bars, riverside bike paths, and contemporary art spaces like the Kunsthalle Weishaupt. It feels more relaxed and less touristy than the old town.

A quiet, leafy district built around a former Poor Clares monastery, Söflingen Abbey, now offering a calmer, residential alternative to central Ulm. Local bakeries and small parks give it a village-like feel despite being minutes from downtown.

A hillside district anchored by the University of Ulm and its associated science park, with sweeping views back over the city and the Danube valley. It's quiet and largely residential, popular with students and academics rather than tourists.

water.note: German tap water is safe and strictly regulated.

transit.hours: Approximately 5am to midnight, with reduced night-bus service on weekends
transit.pay: SWU ticket machines, apps (DB Navigator, SWU), or contactless card; day passes available
transit.note: The tram network was expanded in recent years and connects the Hauptbahnhof, Altstadt, and university district efficiently

train: Ulm Hauptbahnhof sits on the ICE high-speed line between Stuttgart and Munich, roughly 40 min and 1 hr away respectively
bus: FlixBus and regional buses connect Ulm to nearby cities and the airports

car.idp: Not required for EU/UK/US short stays

tip.r: Round the bill up or add roughly 5-10% at restaurants; tell the server the total including tip rather than leaving cash on the table
